## ROCMICS

Teneille's data analysis repository is available at <https://github.com/Teneille97/rocmics>.

## Pipette method

Soil samples were dispersed by ultrasonication at low, medium and high energy to disperse aggregates to an increasing degree, where the highest energy level is assumed to disperse the aggregates completely. 

After sonication, the samples were mixed in sedimentation cylinders and the heavier particles were allowed to settle for several hours, such that only the clay fraction remained in suspension. This was sampled, dried and weighed to determine the % clay released from aggregates at different energy levels.

## Results

At highest energy level, most treatments release more clay than at lower energy levels (but not Bolsdorfer). Energy released at highest energy level, had moderate positive correlation with oPOM and negative correlation with MAOM (fractions determined by density fractionation).

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| label: Sedimentation
#| warning: FALSE


# SOM decomposition models for Malle soil

# ============================================================
# LOAD LIBRARIES
# ============================================================

library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(patchwork)
library(emmeans)
library(stringr)


# ============================================================
# DATA CLEANING
# ============================================================

radiocarbon_samples <- read.csv(
  here("outputs", "radiocarbon_samples.csv")
)

aggstab_h2o <- read.csv(
  here("outputs", "aggstab_h2o.csv")
)

SOM_fraction_data <- radiocarbon_samples[
  radiocarbon_samples$Sampling_year == "2026",
]


# ============================================================
# LOAD PIPETTE DATA
# ============================================================

pipette_rawdata <- read.csv(
  here("csv_files", "Pipette_rawdata.csv")
)


# ============================================================
# LOAD METADATA
# ============================================================

metadata <- read.csv(
  here("csv_files", "treatment_names.csv")
) %>%
  mutate(
    analysis_group = case_when(
      Treatment == "Control" ~ "Control",
      Treatment == "Eifelgold_50" ~ "Eifelgold_50",
      Treatment == "Bolsdorfer_50" ~ "Bolsdorfer_50",
      Treatment == "Lime_2" ~ "Lime_2",
      Treatment == "Huhnerberg_50" ~ "Huhnerberg_50",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )


# ============================================================
# JOIN METADATA TO PIPETTE DATA
# ============================================================

pipette_with_metadata <- merge(
  pipette_rawdata,
  metadata,
  by.x = "Sample",
  by.y = "sample",
  all.x = TRUE
)

# Remove clay outlier: Sample 16, Rep B, Energy III
pipette_with_metadata <- pipette_with_metadata %>%
  filter(
    !(Sample == 16 & Rep == "b" & Energy == "iii")
  ) %>%
  filter(
    !(X.clay_corrected ==- 0)
  )


# ============================================================
# LOAD SOM FRACTION DATA
# ============================================================

SOM_wide <- SOM_fraction_data %>%
  mutate(
    sample_id = as.integer(
      str_extract(sample, "^[0-9]+")
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = sample_id,
    names_from = SOM_fraction,
    values_from = fraction_prop
  )


# ============================================================
# JOIN SOM FRACTIONS
# ============================================================

pipette_with_metadata <- pipette_with_metadata %>%
  left_join(
    SOM_wide,
    by = c("Sample" = "sample_id")
  )


# ============================================================
# PREPARE AGGREGATE STABILITY DATA
# ============================================================

aggstab_fractions <- aggstab_h2o %>%
  filter(
    fraction_type %in% c(
      ">0.25",
      ">0.063",
      "<0.063"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    sample,
    fraction_type
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    fraction_mean = mean(
      fraction,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fraction_type = case_when(
      fraction_type == ">0.25" ~ "fraction_more_0.25",
      fraction_type == ">0.063" ~ "fraction_more_0.063",
      fraction_type == "<0.063" ~ "fraction_less_0.063"
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = fraction_type,
    values_from = fraction_mean
  ) %>%
  rename(
    sample_id = sample
  )


# ============================================================
# JOIN AGGREGATE STABILITY DATA
# ============================================================

pipette_with_metadata <- pipette_with_metadata %>%
  left_join(
    aggstab_fractions,
    by = c("Sample" = "sample_id")
  )

pipette_with_metadata$Treatment<-as.factor(pipette_with_metadata$Treatment)

# clay normalized to oPOM

pipette_with_metadata <- pipette_with_metadata %>%
  mutate(
    clay_to_oPOM_ratio =
      X.clay_corrected / oPOM
  )

# ============================================================
# SUMMARISE
# ============================================================

summary_data <- pipette_with_metadata %>%
  group_by(
    Treatment,
    Energy
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    
    mean_X.clay_corrected = mean(
      X.clay_corrected,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    sd_X.clay_corrected = sd(
      X.clay_corrected,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    n = sum(
      !is.na(X.clay_corrected)
    ),
    
    Bulk_prop = mean(
      Bulk,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    fPOM_prop = mean(
      fPOM,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    oPOM_prop = mean(
      oPOM,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    MAOM_prop = mean(
      MAOM,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    clay_to_oPOM_ratio = mean(
      X.clay_corrected/oPOM,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    fraction_more_0.25 = mean(
      fraction_more_0.25,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    fraction_more_0.063 = mean(
      fraction_more_0.063,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    fraction_less_0.063 = mean(
      fraction_less_0.063,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    
    .groups = "drop"
  )

summary_data$Treatment<-as.factor(summary_data$Treatment)

# ============================================================
# FILTER INTO TREATMENT AND DOSE-RESPONSE DATAFRAMES
# ============================================================

pipette_app50_df <- summary_data %>%
  filter(
    !str_detect(Treatment, "Huhnerberg") |
      Treatment == "Huhnerberg_50"
  )
pipette_app50_df$Treatment<-as.factor(pipette_app50_df$Treatment)

dose_response_df <- summary_data %>%
  filter(
    Treatment == "Control" |
      str_detect(Treatment, "Huhnerberg")
  )
dose_response_df$Treatment<-as.factor(dose_response_df$Treatment)


# ============================================================
# PLOT CLAY
# ============================================================

ggplot(
  pipette_app50_df,
  aes(
    x = Energy,
    y = mean_X.clay_corrected,
    fill = Energy
  )
) +
  geom_col(
    color = "black",
    alpha = 0.8,
    width = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = pmax(
        0,
        mean_X.clay_corrected - sd_X.clay_corrected
      ),
      ymax = mean_X.clay_corrected + sd_X.clay_corrected
    ),
    width = 0.2,
    linewidth = 0.6
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ Treatment) +
  labs(
    x = "Energy Level",
    y = "Mean % Clay (Corrected)",
    title = "Mean % Clay ± SD by Energy Level Across Treatments"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none"
  )


# ============================================================
# filter out dose-response
# ============================================================
pipette_with_metadata_50 <- pipette_with_metadata %>%
  filter(
    !str_detect(Treatment, "Huhnerberg") |
      Treatment == "Huhnerberg_50"
  )


# ============================================================
# CORRELATION HEATMAPS: CONSISTENT SAMPLE-LEVEL DATA
# ============================================================

# 1. Calculate the Energy III - Energy I difference per sample
clay_difference_data <- pipette_with_metadata_50 %>%
  filter(Energy %in% c("i", "iii")) %>%
  group_by(Sample, Energy) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_clay = mean(X.clay_corrected, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Energy,
    values_from = mean_clay,
    names_prefix = "clay_energy_"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    clay_difference = clay_energy_iii - clay_energy_i
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample, clay_difference)


# 2. Create one row per sample for sample-level variables
sample_level_data <- pipette_with_metadata_50 %>%
  group_by(Sample) %>%
  summarise(
    Treatment = first(Treatment),
    oPOM = first(oPOM),
    MAOM = first(MAOM),
    fraction_more_0.25 = first(fraction_more_0.25),
    fraction_more_0.063 = first(fraction_more_0.063),
    fraction_less_0.063 = first(fraction_less_0.063),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(clay_difference_data, by = "Sample")


# 3. Function to create heatmaps with consistent sample-level data
make_correlation_heatmap <- function(
    data,
    energy,
    title_text
) {
  
  # Select clay release for the requested energy
  clay_energy_data <- pipette_with_metadata_50 %>%
    filter(Energy == energy) %>%
    group_by(Sample) %>%
    summarise(
      X.clay_corrected = mean(
        X.clay_corrected,
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  # Join the energy-specific clay values to the same sample-level data
  correlation_data <- data %>%
    dplyr::select(
      Sample,
      oPOM,
      MAOM,
      fraction_more_0.25,
      fraction_more_0.063,
      fraction_less_0.063
    ) %>%
    left_join(clay_energy_data, by = "Sample") %>%
    dplyr::select(
      X.clay_corrected,
      oPOM,
      MAOM,
      fraction_more_0.25,
      fraction_more_0.063,
      fraction_less_0.063
    )
  
  cor_matrix <- cor(
    correlation_data,
    method = "spearman",
    use = "pairwise.complete.obs"
  )
  
  cor_long <- as.data.frame(cor_matrix) %>%
    mutate(variable1 = rownames(.)) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = -variable1,
      names_to = "variable2",
      values_to = "correlation"
    )
  
  variable_order <- c(
    "X.clay_corrected",
    "oPOM",
    "MAOM",
    "fraction_more_0.25",
    "fraction_more_0.063",
    "fraction_less_0.063"
  )
  
  variable_labels <- c(
    X.clay_corrected = "Clay released (%)",
    oPOM = "oPOM",
    MAOM = "MAOM",
    fraction_more_0.25 = ">0.25 mm",
    fraction_more_0.063 = ">0.063 mm",
    fraction_less_0.063 = "<0.063 mm"
  )
  
  cor_long <- cor_long %>%
    mutate(
      variable1 = factor(variable1, levels = variable_order),
      variable2 = factor(variable2, levels = variable_order)
    )
  
  ggplot(
    cor_long,
    aes(x = variable1, y = variable2, fill = correlation)
  ) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white") +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", correlation)),
      size = 3.2
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      limits = c(-1, 1),
      midpoint = 0,
      name = "Spearman\n\u03C1"
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = variable_labels) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = variable_labels) +
    coord_equal() +
    labs(
      title = title_text,
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
      panel.grid = element_blank()
    )
}


# 4. Create the heatmap
correlation_heatmap_Energy_III <- make_correlation_heatmap(
  sample_level_data,
  energy = "iii",
  title_text = "Correlations at Energy III (App50 Subset)"
)

correlation_heatmap_Energy_III

```
